newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe will lose if Lithuania kept out - president.
newsitem.headline: Europe will lose if Lithuania kept out - president.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas urged Western Europe on Thursday to consider the price of not granting EU and NATO membership to his country rather than the cost of doing so.
"We hear a lot about the cost, but let's look at the price of a redivision of the Baltic sea," he told a meeting of the European Parliament's foreign and security committee.
Brazauskas, who also held talks at the Western European Union (WEU), the EU's designated defence wing, said Europe should not repeat the mistakes of history.

Lithuania, along with the other Baltic states Latvia and Estonia, was forcibly annexed into the Soviet Union under the 1940 Moscow-Nazi pact. They did not regain independence until after the collapse of the Soviet Union.
"The Baltic states must not be left out again," he told reporters later, adding that even partial exclusion played into the hands of countries which believed in "zones of influence".
Moscow opposes the enlargement of NATO eastwards in general, but flatly rejects it for the former Soviet republics -- an increasingly delicate issue for the West.
On Monday, Brazauskas said he wanted his country to be among the first new members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

"Lithuania should be among the first new members... Lithuania is ready to be a reliable and active member. You should not expect us to be troublemakers," he said at a meeting with the Atlantic Alliance's 16 ambassadors.

NATO is expected to invite some countries of former communist central and eastern Europe to join the alliance at a special summit next year. Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are the favourites.
